bib.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

question: Can sharing keys and values across attention heads cut the memory-bandwidth cost of incremental Transformer decoding without hurting quality?
hypothesis: Removing the heads dimension from K and V reduces the n/d memory-to-compute term by a factor of h and so speeds incremental decoding with minor quality loss.
contributions: Performance analysis of batched and incremental multi-head attention showing memory access to arithmetic ratio of Theta(n/d + 1/b)
Multi-query attention: heads share one set of keys and values
Experiments on WMT14 EN-DE and Billion-Word LM showing large decode speedup and small quality loss

method.summary: Replace every attention layer (encoder self, decoder self, encoder-decoder) with multi-query attention, which keeps h query heads but one shared K and V, and widen the feed-forward layer to keep parameters equal. Compare quality and amortized training and inference time against multi-head, local attention and reduced-h/dk/dv variants.
method.task: machine translation (WMT14 EN-DE) and language modelling (Billion-Word)

datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-German
datasets.split: dev (wmt13 sacrebleu set) for BLEU and perplexity; test (wmt14) for final BLEU
datasets.preprocessing: multiple training sentences concatenated to 256-token sequences

models.name: local variants
models.architecture: decoder self-attention limited to current and previous 31 positions

models.name: reduced h/dk/dv variants
models.architecture: multi-head with h in 1,2,4,8 and dk=dv in 128,64,32,16

training.batch_size: MT: 128 examples of 256 input + 256 target tokens; LM: 64K tokens
training.wall_clock: about 2 hours per MT model; about 3 hours per LM model

other.note: learning rates, dropout, label smoothing are deferred to a configuration link marked [to be added before publication]

inference.decoding: greedy maximum-likelihood (dev); greedy and beam 4 with alpha 0.6 (test)
inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds reported

parameters.padding: fixed shapes with padding and masking, so each decode step takes the same time

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: sacrebleu -t wmt13 -l en-de -tok intl on dev; -t wmt14 on test

metrics.name: amortized time
metrics.definition: step or pass time divided by number of tokens

baselines: fewer heads and smaller dk, dv
eval.protocol: single runs, no significance test or seeds reported

availability.code: configuration link left as [to be added before publication]

results.claim: Multi-query cuts amortized incremental decoder time per token about 12x versus multi-head (greedy).
results.setup: WMT14 EN-DE, 211M-param 6-layer encoder-decoder, incremental greedy inference on one TPUv2 (8 cores), batch 1024, source and target length 128
results.quote: for amortized per-token costs of 1.5µs and 3.8µs respectively

results.claim: Multi-query decoding under beam-4 search is about 6x faster in the decoder.
results.table: Table 2, row multi-query, column Beam-4 Search enc. + dec.

results.claim: Multi-query decoder step takes 3.9 ms against 47 ms for multi-head.
results.setup: WMT14 EN-DE, 211M-param 6-layer encoder-decoder, incremental greedy inference on one TPUv2 (8 cores), batch 1024, source and target length 128

results.claim: Multi-query encoder pass is slightly faster, 195 ms versus 222 ms.
results.setup: WMT14 EN-DE, 211M-param 6-layer encoder-decoder, incremental greedy inference on one TPUv2 (8 cores), batch 1024, source and target length 128

results.claim: Training step cost is essentially unchanged: 13.0 vs 13.2 us per token.
results.setup: one TPUv2 (8 cores), 32,768 input + 32,768 target tokens per step
results.table: Table 2, row multi-query, column Training enc. + dec.

results.claim: Dev BLEU is 0.2 lower for multi-query (greedy).
Dev ln(PPL) is 1.439 for multi-query against 1.424 for multi-head.
Multi-query had the highest test BLEU with beam-4 decoding.
results.quote: actually had the highest BLEU score (28.5) with beam-4 decoding

results.claim: Cutting heads to 1 costs far more quality than multi-query (dev BLEU 25.8).
results.setup: WMT14 EN-DE dev, h=1, dk=dv=128, dff 6784
results.table: Table 1, row multi-head h=1, column BLEU (dev)

results.claim: Memory access to arithmetic ratio of incremental multi-head attention is Theta(n/d + 1/b); multi-query removes a factor h from the n/d term.

limits: Only one small setup: 211M WMT14 EN-DE and 192M Billion-Word models trained for hours; no large-scale or decoder-only generation quality tests.
Speed test uses fixed padded shapes, so every decode step costs the same; the author notes growing tensors could save time early in the sequence.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; training hyperparameters deferred to a link marked to be added before publication.
Quality drop is small but present (dev BLEU 26.7 to 26.5, LM PPL 29.9 to 30.2).

terms.definition: identical to multi-head attention except that the different heads share a single set of keys and values
